questions.question: The 73rd constitutional amendment deals with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panchayati Raj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992** was enacted to institutionalize **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)**, providing them with constitutional status and protection.
 
• This amendment inserted a new **Part IX** into the Constitution of India, titled **The Panchayats**, which encompasses provisions from **Article 243 to 243-O**.
 
• It also introduced the **11th Schedule**, which details **29 functional items** or subjects, such as **agriculture**, **land improvement**, and **minor irrigation**, that fall under the jurisdiction of Panchayats.
 
• The act gave practical shape to **Article 40** of the **Directive Principles of State Policy**, which directs the State to organize village panchayats as units of **self-government**.
 
• It mandates a **three-tier system** of Panchayati Raj in every state: **Gram Panchayat** (village level), **Panchayat Samiti** (intermediate level), and **Zila Parishad** (district level).
 
• The act provides for mandatory **reservation of seats** for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in proportion to their population, and at least **one-third reservation** for **women**.
 
• To ensure financial and electoral autonomy, the act established the **State Finance Commission** to review financial positions and the **State Election Commission** to conduct fair elections every **five years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anti-defection**:

 
 
• Introduced by the **52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985** to prevent political defections.
 
• It added the **10th Schedule**, which lays down the process by which legislators may be disqualified on grounds of defection.
 
 
 
• **Tribunals**:
 
 
• Constitutional status was provided by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• It added **Part XIV-A**, containing **Article 323A** for administrative tribunals and **Article 323B** for other matters.
 
 
 
• **Cooperative Societies**:
 
 
• Given constitutional status through the **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011**.
 
• It added **Part IX-B** and included the right to form cooperatives as a **Fundamental Right** under **Article 19(1)(c)**.

questions.question: The first woman governor of an Indian state was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarojini Naidu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sarojini Naidu** was appointed as the **Governor of the United Provinces** (currently known as **Uttar Pradesh**) on **August 15, 1947**, following India's independence.
 
• She held this prestigious constitutional office until her death on **March 2, 1949**, making her the **first woman** to serve as a **Governor** in the history of independent India.
 
• Commonly known as the **Nightingale of India** (Bharat Kokila), she was a prolific **poet** and a major political figure in the **Indian National Movement**.
 
• In **1925**, she became the **first Indian woman** to be elected as the **President of the Indian National Congress** during its **Kanpur Session**.
 
• She was a close associate of **Mahatma Gandhi** and played a significant role during the **Civil Disobedience Movement**, including the **Dandi March** and the **Dharasana Satyagraha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indira Gandhi**:

 
 
• She was the **first woman Prime Minister of India**, serving from **1966 to 1977** and again from **1980 until 1984**.
 
• She was the first woman to be honored with the **Bharat Ratna** in **1971** for her leadership during the **Indo-Pakistani War**.
 
 
 
• **Sucheta Kripalani**:
 
 
• She became the **first woman Chief Minister** of an Indian state, leading the government of **Uttar Pradesh** from **1963 to 1967**.
 
• She was a member of the **Constituent Assembly** and founded the **All India Mahila Congress** in **1940**.
 
 
 
• **Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit**:
 
 
• She was the **first woman President of the United Nations General Assembly**, elected in **1953**.
 
• She served as a prominent **diplomat** and was the sister of India's first Prime Minister, **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

questions.question: How many pollutants are measured under India's Air Quality Index (AQI)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Air Quality Index (AQI)** was launched in **September 2014** in New Delhi under the **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** to provide a simplified health-related air quality status to the public.
 
• Developed by the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** in consultation with **IIT Kanpur** and medical professionals, it follows the mantra of **One Number-One Colour-One Description**.
 
• The index measures **eight major pollutants** for which short-term national standards have been prescribed. These are **Particulate Matter (PM10)**, **Particulate Matter (PM2.5)**, **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂)**, **Sulphur Dioxide (SO₂)**, **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**, **Ozone (O₃)**, **Ammonia (NH₃)**, and **Lead (Pb)**.
 
• The **AQI** calculation is based on the **24-hour average** concentration for most pollutants, except for **Ozone** and **Carbon Monoxide**, which are monitored on an **8-hour average** basis to better reflect immediate health impacts.
 
• The overall AQI for a location is determined by the **sub-index** of the pollutant that is most prominent (the pollutant with the highest concentration relative to its standard) on a given day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **AQI Categories and Health Impact**:

 
 
• **Good (0−50)**: Minimal health impact.
 
• **Satisfactory (51−100)**: May cause minor breathing discomfort to sensitive individuals.
 
• **Moderately Polluted (101−200)**: May cause breathing discomfort to people with asthma and heart diseases.
 
• **Poor (201−300)**: Causes breathing discomfort to most people on prolonged exposure.
 
• **Very Poor (301−400)**: Leads to respiratory illness upon prolonged exposure.
 
• **Severe (401−500)**: Affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing respiratory or cardiovascular ailments.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with NAAQS**:
 
 
• While the AQI monitors **8 pollutants**, the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)** officially monitor **12 pollutants**.
 
• The four pollutants included in NAAQS but excluded from daily AQI reporting are **Benzene**, **Benzo(a)pyrene**, **Arsenic**, and **Nickel**, as they are primarily monitored for long-term (annual) chronic exposure rather than short-term spikes.

questions.question: Freedom to make life choices in the Happiness Index refers to:

options.text: People's perception of having control over life decisions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**People's perception of having control over life decisions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Happiness Report** utilizes six key variables to explain the variation in happiness across different nations, one of which is the **Freedom to make life choices**.
 
• This specific metric is defined as the national average of binary responses (0 or 1) to the **Gallup World Poll** question: 'Are you satisfied or dissatisfied with your freedom to choose what you do with your life?'.
 
• It represents an individual's **subjective perception** of their own **autonomy** and the extent to which they feel they have the agency to steer their own life path without undue restriction.
 
• Unlike objective measures of **civil liberties** or **legal rights**, this indicator focuses on the internal psychological state of feeling 'free', which is highly correlated with overall **life satisfaction**.
 
• Data collected indicates that a strong sense of personal agency is a fundamental pillar of human well-being, often ranking as more significant than absolute income in developed economies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Happiness Index** is published annually by the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**.
 
• The index is calculated using a three-year average of data, primarily employing the **Cantril Ladder**, where respondents rate their lives on a scale from 0 to 10.
 
• Other core variables in the report include:
 
 
• **GDP per Capita**: A measure of the average **economic output** per person, adjusted for **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)**.
 
• **Social Support**: Evaluated by asking if citizens have relatives or friends they can count on during trouble.
 
• **Healthy Life Expectancy**: Extracted from **World Health Organization (WHO)** data, reflecting physical health and longevity.
 
• **Generosity**: Calculated based on the residual of average responses to questions regarding donating money to charity.
 
• **Perceptions of Corruption**: Measured by the perceived level of corruption in government and business sectors.

questions.question: Which state hosted the 37th National Games of India in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **37th edition** of the **National Games of India** was officially held in the state of **Goa** from **October 26 to November 9, 2023**.
 
• This was the **first time** that Goa hosted the prestigious multi-sport event, which saw participation from over **10,000 athletes** representing all **28 states**, **8 Union Territories**, and the **Services Sports Control Board (SSCB)**.
 
• The games were inaugurated by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** at the **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium** located in **Fatorda**, South Goa.
 
• The official **mascot** for the event was named **Moga**, an **Indian Bison (Gaur)**, which is the state animal of Goa; the name **Moga** is derived from the **Konkani** word for love or affection.
 
• The competition featured a record **43 sporting disciplines**, including the debut of sports such as **Beach Football**, **Rollball**, **Golf**, **Sepaktakraw**, **Kalaripayattu**, **Lagori**, and **Pencak Silat**.
 
• The events were organized across five main Goan cities: **Panaji**, **Margao**, **Mapusa**, **Ponda**, and **Vasco**, with **Cycling** and **Golf** being the only events held in **New Delhi** due to infrastructure requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Performance and Awards:**

 
 
• **Maharashtra** finished at the top of the medal tally with a total of **228 medals** (80 gold, 69 silver, and 79 bronze), successfully claiming the **Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy**.
 
• The **Services Sports Control Board (SSCB)** secured the second position with **66 gold medals**, while **Haryana** finished third with **62 gold medals**.
 
• **Srihari Nataraj**, a swimmer from **Karnataka**, was adjudged the **Best Male Athlete** for winning **8 gold**, **1 silver**, and **1 bronze** medal.
 
• **Sanyukta Prashen Kale** and **Pranati Nayak**, both gymnasts, were jointly named the **Best Female Athlete**.
 
 
 
• **Context and History:**
 
 
• The previous **36th National Games** were hosted by **Gujarat** in **2022** after a significant delay due to the pandemic.
 
• The **38th edition** of the National Games is scheduled to be held in the state of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• The National Games of India are modeled after the **Olympics** and are organized by the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)** to promote sports at the grassroots level and identify national talent.

questions.question: By 1990, India's external debt had become:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Very high, leading to crisis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the late **1980s**, India faced a severe **macroeconomic imbalance** due to persistent **fiscal deficits**, which climbed to nearly **8.4% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** by **1990-91**.
 
• The government increasingly relied on **external commercial borrowings** and short-term debt to bridge the gap between revenue and expenditure, leading to a massive accumulation of **external debt**.
 
• By **1990**, India's external debt had reached approximately **$72 billion**, and the **debt-service ratio** surged to over **35%**, meaning more than one-third of export earnings went solely toward interest payments.
 
• This unsustainable debt level triggered a **Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis**, as the **foreign exchange reserves** plummeted to a critical low of about **$1.2 billion**.
 
• These reserves were sufficient to finance essential **imports** (like petroleum and fertilizers) for only about **two weeks**, pushing the country toward **sovereign default**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 1991 economic crisis was exacerbated by external factors and required significant policy shifts:
 
 
• **Gulf War (1990)**: The conflict caused **crude oil prices** to skyrocket and led to a sharp decline in **remittances** from Indian workers in the Middle East, further draining foreign exchange.
 
• **IMF Intervention**: To secure an emergency loan from the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**, the **Reserve Bank of India** had to airlift **47 tonnes of gold** to the **Bank of England** as collateral.
 
• **New Economic Policy**: The crisis served as a catalyst for the **July 1991 reforms**, introducing **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** to restructure the Indian economy.

questions.question: Alvars saints were devoted to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vishnu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Alvars** were a group of **Tamil poet-saints** from **South India** who flourished between the **6th and 9th centuries CE**.
 
• They were wandering singers who were completely **immersed** in their devotion to **Lord Vishnu** and his diverse incarnations, such as **Krishna** and **Rama**.
 
• The term **Alvar** translates to 'one who is **deeply immersed**' in the ocean of **divine love** for the **Supreme Being**.
 
• There were **12 Alvars** in total, including prominent figures like **Nammalvar**, **Periyalvar**, and **Andal**, who was the only female saint in the group.
 
• They played a vital role in initiating the **Bhakti Movement**, making religious devotion accessible to all sections of society regardless of **caste** or **gender**.
 
• Their sacred compositions were compiled by **Nathamuni** into a collection known as the **Nalayira Divya Prabandham**, often hailed as the **Dravida Veda**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nayanars**:

 
 
• These were **63 saints** who were devoted to **Lord Shiva** and were contemporaries of the Alvars.
 
• Their hymns were compiled into the **Thirumurai**, and the first seven volumes are known as the **Tevaram**.
 
 
 
• **Durga**:
 
 
• A principal deity in **Shaktism**, she represents **feminine power** (Shakti) and is revered as the destroyer of evil, specifically the demon **Mahishasura**.
 
 
 
• **Agni and Indra**:
 
 
• **Agni** is the **God of Fire** and acts as a mediator between gods and humans in **Vedic rituals**.
 
• **Indra** is the **King of Gods** and the **God of Thunder** and **Rain**, holding supreme status during the **Rig Vedic period**.

questions.question: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan targets how many tribal villages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**63843**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA)** was approved by the Union Cabinet on **October 2, 2024**, to ensure the holistic development of tribal villages.
 
• The mission specifically targets **63,843 tribal-majority villages** across the country to saturate gaps in social infrastructure and basic facilities.
 
• This massive tribal outreach program covers **549 districts** and **2,740 blocks** across **30 States and Union Territories**.
 
• The scheme is designed to directly benefit more than **5 crore tribal people**, focusing on improving their socio-economic indicators through **inter-ministerial convergence**.
 
• The implementation strategy involves identifying **Scheduled Tribe (ST)** dominated areas where the saturation of government schemes has not yet been achieved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial and Administrative Structure**:

 
 
• The total financial outlay for the mission is **Rs. 79,156 crore**, with the Central Government contributing **Rs. 48,399 crore** and the State Governments providing **Rs. 30,757 crore**.
 
• The mission involves **25 specific interventions** that are implemented through **17 different Central Ministries**.
 
 
 
• **Core Objectives and Legacy**:
 
 
• The program is named after **Bhagwan Birsa Munda**, popularly known as **'Dharti Aaba'** (Father of the Earth), a legendary tribal freedom fighter and folk hero.
 
• It follows the model of the **PM-JANMAN** (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan), which focused on **Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)**.
 
• Key infrastructure targets include the construction of **20 lakh pucca houses**, **25,000 km of roads**, and providing **piped water** to every tribal household.
 
• Education and health initiatives include the establishment of **Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres (TMMCs)** and **Ashram schools**.

questions.question: Which of the following objectives emphasizes ethical living in the Vedic framework?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dharma** is the foundational concept in the **Vedic framework** that refers to **righteousness**, **moral values**, and the **ethical code** of conduct necessary to maintain the balance of the universe.
 
• The term is derived from the **Sanskrit** root **Dhri**, which means to **uphold**, **support**, or **sustain**. It signifies the duties and laws that govern individual actions and social order.
 
• In the context of the **Purusharthas** (the four aims of human life), **Dharma** is considered the most critical because it provides the **ethical framework** within which the other goals must be pursued.
 
• It emphasizes **integrity**, **justice**, and **Satya** (truth), guiding individuals to perform their **Svadharma** (personal duty) in harmony with the **cosmic order**, known as **Rta** in the **Rig Veda**.
 
• By prioritizing **ethical living**, **Dharma** ensures that human behavior leads to both **Abhyudaya** (worldly prosperity) and **Nishreyasa** (spiritual well-being).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Purusharthas** provide a holistic approach to a fulfilling life by balancing material and spiritual needs:

 
 
• **Artha**: This goal focuses on **material prosperity**, wealth, and **economic security**. It is essential for survival and social stability but must be acquired through **righteous means** as defined by **Dharma**.
 
• **Kama**: It represents **desire**, sensory pleasure, **love**, and aesthetic enjoyment. The **Vedas** recognize **Kama** as a natural human urge that should be satisfied within the boundaries of **moral law**.
 
• **Moksha**: This is the **ultimate goal** of human existence, signifying **liberation** from the cycle of birth and death (**Samsara**). It represents the realization of the self (**Atman**) and union with the supreme reality (**Brahman**).

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of voluntary action seen in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Writing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Voluntary actions** are those activities in the human body that are performed under the **conscious control** and will of the individual. These actions are primarily regulated by the **cerebrum**, the largest part of the brain, which processes sensory information and initiates motor impulses.
 
• **Writing** is a classic example of a voluntary action as it involves **conscious thought**, decision-making, and memory. The **motor cortex** in the frontal lobe of the brain sends specific signals through the spinal cord to the skeletal muscles in the **fingers, hand, and wrist** to execute precise movements.
 
• Unlike reflexes, voluntary actions can be initiated, modified, or stopped at any moment based on **environmental stimuli** or personal choice. These actions are learned over time and require a high degree of **neuromuscular coordination** and cognitive processing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Involuntary Actions:** These are spontaneous and automatic responses that do not require conscious thought. They are controlled by the **autonomous nervous system** and the **hindbrain**.

 
 
• **Vomiting:** This is a protective **reflex action** controlled by the **vomit center** located in the **medulla oblongata**. It is an involuntary ejection of stomach contents through the mouth.
 
• **Salivation:** This is an involuntary response to the sight, smell, or taste of food, managed by the **salivary nuclei** in the brainstem to facilitate **digestion**.
 
• **Breathing:** Although it can be modulated voluntarily for short durations, **respiration** is fundamentally an involuntary process driven by the **pons** and **medulla** to maintain **homeostasis** of oxygen and carbon dioxide levels.

questions.question: In Indian constitution, ______ may by law provide for the adjudication of any dispute or complaint with respect to the use, distribution or control of the waters of, or in, any inter-State River or river valley.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 262** of the **Indian Constitution** specifically addresses the **adjudication of disputes** relating to waters of **inter-State rivers** or river valleys.
 
• According to **Article 262(1)**, **Parliament** is the sole authority empowered to make laws providing for the adjudication of any dispute or complaint regarding the **use, distribution, or control** of the waters of any **inter-State river** or river valley.
 
• The **Constitution** further provides under **Article 262(2)** that **Parliament** may, by law, exclude the jurisdiction of the **Supreme Court** or any other court in respect of such water disputes.
 
• This provision was included to ensure that complex **riparian issues** and **inter-state conflicts** are resolved through specialized mechanisms rather than standard judicial litigation, which might be time-consuming or technically limited.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legislative Acts under Article 262**:

 
 
• **Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956**: This Act was enacted to facilitate the creation of **ad-hoc tribunals** (e.g., **Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal**, **Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal**) for the adjudication of inter-state water conflicts.
 
• **River Boards Act, 1956**: This law provides for the establishment of **River Boards** for the regulation and development of **inter-State rivers**, aimed at advising the **Central Government** on coordination and development.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Distribution of Power**:
 
 
• **Entry 17** of the **State List** (List II) gives states power over water supplies, irrigation, and canals.
 
• **Entry 56** of the **Union List** (List I) gives the **Union** power over the regulation and development of **inter-State rivers** and river valleys to the extent declared by **Parliament** to be in the public interest.
 
 
 
• **Other Entities**:
 
 
• The **President**, **Council of Ministers**, and **Union Home Minister** do not possess the constitutional authority to legislate or provide the legal framework for the adjudication of these specific water disputes; their roles are limited to **executive functions** or administrative implementation.

questions.question: Where has the Government of India launched the 5th Marine Census in the "Coastal state fisheries conference 2025"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, and Dairying, **Rajiv Ranjan Singh**, officially launched the **5th Marine Census** during the **Coastal State Fisheries Conference 2025** held in **Mumbai**, Maharashtra.
 
• The census is a massive national-level exercise conducted to gather updated and granular data on the **marine fisheries sector**, which is vital for evidence-based policy formulation and the **blue economy**.
 
• The **Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI)** has been designated as the nodal agency to execute this census, covering the entire **8,118 km coastline** of India, including all maritime states and Union Territories.
 
• This initiative aims to enumerate **fishing families**, fishing craft, and gear, while also assessing the **socio-economic status** of the fishing community to ensure better targeted developmental schemes.
 
• The conference in **Mumbai** served as a platform for **coastal states** to discuss sustainable fishing practices, infrastructure development, and the implementation of the **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI)**:

 
 
• Established in **1947** under the Ministry of Agriculture and later joined the **ICAR** (Indian Council of Agricultural Research) in 1967.
 
• Headquartered in **Kochi**, Kerala, it is the leading organization for **marine fisheries research** in India.
 
 
 
• **Marine Fisheries Census History**:
 
 
• The previous **4th Marine Fisheries Census** was conducted in **2016**, providing data on over **4 million** fisherfolk.
 
• The **5th edition** leverages **digital technology** and mobile applications for real-time data collection and enhanced accuracy.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Fisheries Sector**:
 
 
• India is the **third-largest fish producer** and the **second-largest aquaculture** producer in the world.
 
• The sector contributes significantly to the **Gross Value Added (GVA)** of the Indian economy and provides livelihoods to nearly **28 million people**.

questions.question: Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner come under which union ministry of India?

options.text: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Home Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner (ORGI)** was established in **1961** by the Government of India to provide a permanent foundation for the census organization.
 
• It operates under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)**, which oversees the security and internal policy of the country.
 
• The organization is headed by the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India**, who is typically an officer of the rank of **Joint Secretary** or above from the **Indian Administrative Service (IAS)**.
 
• The primary responsibility of this office is to conduct the **decennial Population Census**, which is authorized under the **Census Act, 1948**.
 
• It is also responsible for the implementation of the **Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969**, which manages the **Civil Registration System (CRS)** across India.
 
• The office plays a critical role in the maintenance of the **National Population Register (NPR)** under the **Citizenship Act, 1955** and the **Linguistic Survey of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI):**

 
 
• MoSPI is the nodal agency for the planned development of the statistical system in the country and manages the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**.
 
• While it conducts major surveys like the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** and computes the **Consumer Price Index (CPI)**, it is not responsible for the population census.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional and Historical Context:**
 
 
• The **Census** is a **Union Subject** listed under **Entry 69** of the **Seventh Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• The first census in India was conducted in **1872** under **Lord Mayo**, but the first synchronous (complete) census took place in **1881** under **Lord Ripon**.
 
• The **Census Commissioner** was a temporary post until the office was made permanent in **1961**.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a fire extinguisher?

options.text: To add more fuel to the fire
To increase the temperature of the fuel
To increase the supply of air
To cut off the supply of air, reduce the temperature of the fuel, or both

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To cut off the supply of air, reduce the temperature of the fuel, or both**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fire is a chemical reaction known as **combustion**, which requires three fundamental components typically represented as the **Fire Triangle**: **Fuel** (combustible material), **Heat** (to reach ignition temperature), and **Oxygen** (usually from air).
 
• The fundamental principle of a **fire extinguisher** is to disrupt this **Fire Triangle** by removing or neutralizing one or more of its legs.
 
• Extinguishers like **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)** work primarily by **displacing oxygen**. Since CO2 is heavier than air, it settles over the fire, creating a blanket that **cuts off the air supply** necessary for combustion.
 
• Water-based extinguishers function primarily by **absorbing heat** from the burning fuel, cooling it down below its **flash point** or **ignition temperature** to stop the reaction.
 
• Dry chemical extinguishers use agents like **Monoammonium Phosphate** to both smother the fire and interrupt the **chemical chain reaction** that sustains the flame.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fire extinguishers are categorized based on the types of fires they are designed to combat:
 
 
• **Class A**: Used for **ordinary solid combustibles** such as wood, paper, and textiles.
 
• **Class B**: Designed for **flammable liquids** like petrol, oil, and paint.
 
• **Class C**: Suitable for fires involving **flammable gases** like methane or propane.
 
• **Class D**: Specialized for **combustible metals** like magnesium or potassium.
 
• **Electrical Fires**: Often handled by non-conductive agents like **CO2** or **Halon** to prevent electrocution.
 
 
 
• The **PASS technique** is the standard operating procedure for using a portable fire extinguisher: **Pull** the pin, **Aim** at the base of the fire, **Squeeze** the trigger, and **Sweep** the nozzle from side to side.

questions.question: In the context of money supply in India, which of the following is NOT the Quantitative tool of Reserve bank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moral suasion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** manages the **money supply** and **inflation** in the Indian economy through its **Monetary Policy**, which utilizes two types of instruments: **Quantitative** and **Qualitative**.
 
• **Quantitative tools** (General tools) are intended to regulate the total volume of **credit** and **liquidity** available in the banking system without discriminating between the sectors that receive the credit.
 
• **Qualitative tools** (Selective tools) are used to regulate the **direction** and **purpose** of credit flow toward specific sectors of the economy, such as agriculture or priority sectors.
 
• **Moral suasion** is a **Qualitative instrument** where the **RBI** uses persuasion, informal suggestions, or psychological pressure on **commercial banks** to align their lending activities with the central bank’s economic objectives.
 
• Unlike **Quantitative tools**, **Moral suasion** does not involve mandatory legal requirements or immediate changes in interest rates but relies on the **cooperation** of the banking community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quantitative Tools of RBI**:

 
 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**: It is the percentage of **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** that commercial banks are legally required to maintain as **cash reserves** with the **RBI**.
 
• **Bank Rate**: This is the standard rate at which the **RBI** is prepared to buy or rediscount **bills of exchange** or other commercial papers, acting as a long-term interest rate signal for the economy.
 
• **Open Market Operations (OMO)**: This involves the simultaneous buying and selling of **Government Securities (G-Secs)** by the **RBI** to either inject liquidity into or absorb excess liquidity from the market.
 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**: The minimum percentage of deposits that a bank must maintain in the form of **liquid assets** like gold or unencumbered government securities.
 
 
 
• **Other Qualitative Tools**:
 
 
• **Margin Requirements**: Adjusting the difference between the **market value** of a security and the **loan amount** granted against it.
 
• **Rationing of Credit**: Fixing a **ceiling** or maximum limit on credit for specific industries or sectors.

questions.question: The 11th BRICS parliamentary forum was held in ____ in June 2025.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brasilia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **11th BRICS Parliamentary Forum** is scheduled to be convened in **Brasilia**, **Brazil**, in **June 2025**.
 
• The hosting of this forum aligns with the **rotating presidency** of the BRICS group, where **Brazil** officially assumes the chairmanship for the year **2025**, succeeding the **Russian Federation**.
 
• This forum serves as a primary platform for **inter-parliamentary cooperation**, enabling heads of legislative bodies from member states to discuss **multilateralism**, **global security**, and **sustainable development**.
 
• The **10th BRICS Parliamentary Forum** took place in **St. Petersburg**, **Russia**, in **July 2024**, where members emphasized the importance of **legislative diplomacy** in a multipolar world.
 
• As the host nation, **Brazil** is responsible for coordinating the agenda, which typically includes the **17th BRICS Summit** and various high-level ministerial meetings throughout the year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BRICS Membership and Expansion**:

 
 
• Founded in **2006** as **BRIC** (Brazil, Russia, India, China) and joined by **South Africa** in **2010**, the group represents a significant portion of **global economic output**.
 
• Effective **January 1, 2024**, the bloc expanded to include **Egypt**, **Ethiopia**, **Iran**, and the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)**.
 
• The 2025 meetings in **Brasilia** will be among the first major gatherings to fully integrate the **legislative representatives** of these newly admitted nations.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Objectives**:
 
 
• The forum aims to strengthen the **New Development Bank (NDB)** and promote the use of **local currencies** in international trade to reduce dependence on the **US Dollar**.
 
• Legislative cooperation within **BRICS** often focuses on reforming **international financial institutions** like the **IMF** and **World Bank** to reflect the current **global economic landscape**.
 
 
 
• **Host City Significance**:
 
 
• **Brasilia**, the **federal capital** of Brazil, is the seat of the **National Congress of Brazil**, making it the strategic venue for high-level **parliamentary negotiations**.

questions.question: 'A Shot at History: My Obsessive Journey to Olympic Gold' is the autobiography of _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhinav Bindra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A Shot at History: My Obsessive Journey to Olympic Gold** is the official autobiography of the renowned Indian shooter **Abhinav Bindra**, published in **2011**.
 
• The book was co-authored by the acclaimed sports journalist **Rohit Brijnath** and provides a deep dive into the mental and physical rigors of elite competitive shooting.
 
• The narrative focuses on Bindra's journey to winning India's first-ever **individual Olympic gold medal** in the **10m Air Rifle** event at the **2008 Beijing Olympics**.
 
• It highlights his **obsessive pursuit of perfection**, detailing unique training methods such as commando training, brain mapping, and his struggle with a career-threatening back injury.
 
• The autobiography is considered a seminal work in Indian sports literature for its honest portrayal of the isolation and pressure faced by Olympic athletes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neeraj Chopra**:

 
 
• He is an Indian **Javelin Thrower** who made history by winning the gold medal at the **2020 Tokyo Olympics**.
 
• He is the second Indian, after **Abhinav Bindra**, to win an individual Olympic gold and the first from independent India to win a medal in **Athletics**.
 
 
 
• **Gagan Narang**:
 
 
• An Indian shooter who specialized in the **Air Rifle** category.
 
• He won the **Bronze medal** in the **Men's 10m Air Rifle** event at the **2012 London Olympics** and has won multiple gold medals in **Commonwealth Games**.
 
 
 
• **Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore**:
 
 
• A former professional shooter and retired **Indian Army** officer.
 
• He won the **Silver medal** in the **Men's Double Trap** event at the **2004 Athens Olympics**, which was India's first individual silver medal since independence.

questions.question: Till Paris Olympics 2024, in which year India has the highest medal tally in any single Olympics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2020**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India recorded its best-ever performance in Olympic history at the **Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics** (held in 2021), where the contingent won a total of **7 medals**.
 
• The **medal distribution** for the Tokyo 2020 Games included **1 Gold**, **2 Silver**, and **4 Bronze** medals, placing India at the **48th position** in the global medal standings.
 
• **Neeraj Chopra** created history by winning the **Gold medal** in the **Men’s Javelin Throw** with a massive throw of **87.58 meters**, becoming the first Indian to win a track and field gold.
 
• The previous record for the highest medal tally was **6 medals**, which was set during the **London 2012 Olympics**.
 
• The **7 medalists** from Tokyo 2020 include **Neeraj Chopra** (Gold), **Mirabai Chanu** (Silver), **Ravi Kumar Dahiya** (Silver), **P.V. Sindhu** (Bronze), **Lovlina Borgohain** (Bronze), **Bajrang Punia** (Bronze), and the **Indian Men’s Hockey Team** (Bronze).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **London 2012 Olympics**:

 
 
• India won **6 medals** (2 Silver and 4 Bronze). Notable winners were **Vijay Kumar** and **Sushil Kumar** (Silver), and **Saina Nehwal**, **Mary Kom**, **Gagan Narang**, and **Yogeshwar Dutt** (Bronze).
 
 
 
• **Paris 2024 Olympics**:
 
 
• India concluded the **Paris 2024** campaign with **6 medals** (1 Silver and 5 Bronze). **Manu Bhaker** became the first athlete from independent India to win **two medals** in a single Olympic edition.
 
 
 
• **Beijing 2008 Olympics**:
 
 
• This edition saw India winning **3 medals**, highlighted by **Abhinav Bindra** winning India’s first-ever individual **Gold medal** in the **10m Air Rifle** event.
 
 
 
• **1932 Los Angeles Olympics**:
 
 
• India won a **Gold medal** in **Field Hockey**. The team, led by **Lal Shah Bokhari**, defeated the USA with a record-breaking score of **24−1** in the final match.
